item.title: Do not feed the animals. Vets explain why hats, coins and shoes can be deadly.
item.description: It's not easy to retrieve foreign objects from animals once ingested. Some things can be grabbed using an endoscope. But if an item gets far into the intestinal tract, surgery isn't always possible.

item.title: What it's like at a climate conference as talks collapse
item.description: After two weeks of negotiations, international climate talks fail to reach an agreement. NPR's Rachel Waldholz was in Turkey for the conference.

item.title: Chicago now has the worst traffic in the U.S. — here's why
item.description: Traffic is bad in many U.S. cities, but Chicago is the worst. Years of construction are causing record delays on the freeway between downtown and O'Hare Airport.

item.title: Medicare looks a bit different in 2027, so don't miss open enrollment
item.description: Open enrollment for Medicare runs through Dec. 7, and there are a few different pitfalls people should watch out for this year. Your drug plan or Medicare Advantage plan could be changing a lot.

item.description: America's fastest-growing source of funding for small businesses is also one of the least regulated. One man has waged a long, lonely fight to recoup its punishing cost.

item.title: Storms expected on both coasts threaten Thanksgiving travel
item.description: The mayor of San Francisco is asking people in the city not to travel unless "absolutely essential." Meanwhile, a storm moving up the Eastern seaboard could also cause travel delays ahead of Thanksgiving.

item.title: Federal jury convicts man of starting the deadly 2025 Palisades Fire in Los Angeles
item.description: Prosecutors argued the defendant, 30-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht, had been "mad at everything" in the days leading up to the January 2025 fire, which killed 12 people.

item.description: After a mistrial earlier in the year, a new jury has found the man accused of starting the devastating 2025 Palisades fire in Los Angeles guilty.

item.title: Senate permitting bill speeds up renewables, divides greens over oil and gas
item.description: A permitting reform bill in the Senate could help speed the development of renewable energy projects, but it's splitting environmentalists over other provisions that help the oil and gas industry.
